paras: The attempted lynching of William Bradway took place on the night of 26 August 1903 in Salem, New Jersey, when a crowd of about 300 people tried to take Bradway, a young Black prisoner, from officers bringing him through the city. Bradway, charged with cutting two Black residents with a razor, was not taken and was held for trial. The only known report is a single sentence in a Salem County weekly.

According to the Woodstown Monitor-Register, Bradway, "a colored youth," was refused when he asked Laura Doran's mother whether he might take her daughter to a camp meeting at the Mt. Pisgah A. M. E. Church in Salem. On the evening of Sunday, 16 August, he was accused of hiding near the path of Doran and her companion Spencer Seibert, slashing Seibert across the face and cutting Doran's arm nearly to the bone.
Bradway fled, and Detective Carney, the sheriff and the chief of police later found him hiding in a hay mow near the Quinton road.

On Wednesday, 26 August, Bradway had a hearing before Justice Smith at Salem. That night, as officers drove him through the upper part of the city, "a mob of about three hundred people gathered about the wagon and tried to get hold of the prisoner, claiming that they wanted to lynch him." The paper did not say how the officers kept him or who was in the crowd.
Justice Smith committed Bradway in default of $1000 bail to the October term of court. No report of a trial, of arrests in the crowd or of any official response was found.

The Monitor-Register ran the story on its front page on 28 August under the headline "A JEALOUS LOVER USES RAZOR ON RIVAL," with decks crediting Detective Carney with running "the Would-be Murderer Down." The account followed the officers' version, called Bradway "a very dangerous character," cited an unproven attempted-murder charge against him in Cumberland County and reported that he had said "his neck was made for the noose." The lynching attempt appeared only near the end, in one sentence without comment.
No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have reported the episode.

bases: A crowd of about 300 tried to take Bradway, a Black prisoner, from officers, claiming it wanted to lynch him; he was not taken or harmed (A1).
The crowd of about 300 sought to lynch Bradway over the razor-assault charge, but the only report shows no one was killed; it was an attempted lynching (A1).
One local weekly, the Woodstown Monitor-Register, is the only report found in either press (A1).

accounts.label: Local weekly (officers' account)
accounts.gist: Bradway cut Seibert and Doran after Doran's mother refused to let him take her to a camp meeting, fled, and was caught hiding in a barn; that night a crowd of about 300 tried to take him from the officers' wagon, claiming it wanted to lynch him.

framing.detail: The Monitor-Register headlined the assault and capture ('A JEALOUS LOVER USES RAZOR ON RIVAL'), called Bradway 'a very dangerous character' and reported the lynching attempt in one sentence without comment.
